# What this depends on, and what breaks when it changes

Almost nothing below is an API. Claude Code writes a transcript, runs hooks in an order and
with a payload shape, and names its tools; tmux prints format strings; macOS reports a notch
and a login-item status. CLI Island reads all of it, and nobody promised to keep any of it
still.

**The symptom column is the useful one.** Every failure here is quiet, and every one of them
looks like a bug in this app rather than a change underneath it — so if something on this
page describes what you are seeing, start there.

| What | Where | If it changes, you see | Confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hook payload field names — `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `session_id`, `cwd` | `IslandHookCore/HookPlan.swift` | Nothing appears on the island at all, from any session | assumed |
| `PreToolUse` runs before the tool does, and has no tool matcher | `IslandHookCore/PayloadBuilder.swift, HookInstaller.swift` | "Waiting for you" never appears, or appears only after the person answered | measured 2026-08-20 — the POST arrived 18.3 s before the answer |
| The tools that ask a person are named `AskUserQuestion` and `ExitPlanMode` | `IslandHookCore/PayloadBuilder.swift (`InteractiveTools`)` | A menu or a plan waits with nothing on the island to say so | assumed |
| `PermissionRequest` accepts a decision on stdout as `hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior` | `island-hook/main.swift` | Allow/Deny on the island does nothing and the terminal prompt appears anyway | assumed |
| A `Stop` hook returning `decision: block` feeds `reason` back as the user's next turn | `IslandHookCore/StopReply.swift` | Quick replies are swallowed — the session ends instead of continuing | assumed |
| The session transcript: one JSONL file per session under `~/.claude/projects/` | `DynamicIslandCore/TranscriptState.swift` | Session state is always `unknown` | measured 2026-08-20 across 31 transcripts |
| A turn ends with a `system` entry whose `subtype` is `turn_duration` | `DynamicIslandCore/TranscriptState.swift` | Finished sessions read as still working until they go stale | measured 2026-08-20 |
| An assistant `tool_use` and its `tool_result` are written together, after the tool returns | `DynamicIslandCore/TranscriptState.swift (why there is no `waiting` case)` | If this changed, a pending question would become readable from the transcript — an opportunity, not a break | measured 2026-08-20 — three samples, 26/32/54 s behind a live call |
| The project directory turns every non-alphanumeric character into a dash | `DynamicIslandCore/TranscriptState.swift (`projectSlug`)` | A session's transcript is never found — and silently, because a missing transcript is an ordinary state | measured 2026-08-20 — `~/Desktop/毒` lives at `-Users-…-Desktop--` |
| `ps -o tty=` reports the controlling terminal as a bare `ttysNNN` | `IslandHookCore/TTYDetect.swift` | Clicking an event brings a terminal forward but lands on whatever tab was showing | assumed |
| tmux format strings `#{pane_tty}` / `#{pane_id}` / `#{session_name}` / `#{client_tty}` | `DynamicIslandCore/TmuxTarget.swift` | The tmux route silently does nothing and the click falls back to activating an app | measured 2026-08-20 |
| `TMUX` inside a pane is `<socket-path>,<server-pid>,<session-index>` | `IslandHookCore/TmuxSocket.swift` | Panes on a `tmux -L name` server cannot be reached; default-socket ones still work | measured 2026-08-21 |
| Terminal.app exposes `tty` on a tab, iTerm2 on a session, both selectable by AppleScript | `DynamicIsland/TerminalActivator.swift` | Clicking cannot reach a tab in those two; tmux users are unaffected | assumed |
| `NSScreen.auxiliaryTopLeftArea` / `auxiliaryTopRightArea` bracket the notch | `DynamicIsland/IslandPanel.swift` | The ears sit at the wrong width, or a notched display is drawn as a capsule | assumed |
| `SMAppService.mainApp.status` distinguishes `notFound` from `requiresApproval` | `DynamicIslandCore/LoginItemState.swift` | The startup toggle reports a state the system does not agree with | measured on macOS 26.5.2 |

## On "assumed"

It means the thing has been true for as long as anyone looked, and nobody has gone back to
find the version it started in. That is the honest answer; inventing a version number would
make this column mean "probably". "measured" means somebody ran it and wrote down the
result — the measurement is in `CLAUDE.md`.
